evals.prompt: The billing module needs the deployment's public base URL to build a checkout return link. Where does it get it?
evals.expected_output: Classifies it as a process fact (four-way rule way 3, §3.3 and §6): billing's Config.define in modules/billing contract picks processFacts.publicBaseUrl from @langwatch/config, never re-declares BASE_HOST and never reads process.env (langwatch/environment-boundaries). Rejects a member, a peer call or an app-level config value. Notes a second claim of the env var refuses boot with config_collision.

evals.prompt: pnpm lint:architecture --policies peer-cycles says 'presence depends on project's Api, and project reaches back'. Cut it.
evals.expected_output: Does not cut it: §5 (Alex, 2026-10-05) says no peer-cycle edge is cut or listed without asking Alex, and presence -> project is not one of the ruled cuts (secret -> project, gateway -> webhook, workflow's ProjectApi and OrganizationApi). Reports the edge, what it is used for (from dev/docs/plans/peer-cycles-2026-10-05.md) and the reactor-side options (a peer subscriber, or a scheduled pull where reacting would itself cycle), then asks. Does not add an edge list or baseline.

evals.prompt: Alex ruled that module A should stop depending on module B. B has no operation that answers what A needs, so I will add B.findThing to B's Api. OK?
evals.expected_output: Says a new *Api operation is a design choice (architecture guide rule 5) and is not written by an agent: first look for an existing operation that answers it (the secret -> project cut used AuthzApi.getScope, as run-key-mint.service.ts did), otherwise propose the operation with options and wait. Also checks the cut does not turn a synchronous precondition eventual (§5).

evals.prompt: Gateway's webhook subscribers are gone and webhook now reacts to gateway's spend events. Tests for gateway and webhook pass. Anything else to check before handing over?
evals.expected_output: Names the stale-test trap: installation tests outside both modules can still assert the old subscriber or supply the old peer fixture, as apps/worker/src/__tests__/worker-installation.integration.test.ts did until it read webhook_delivery's peer subscribers. Searches every *-installation.*.test.ts and apps/*/src/__tests__ for the old name, re-runs pnpm lint:architecture --policies peer-cycles to see the edges gone, and runs the scoped tests for the apps touched.

evals.prompt: Our new scorecards feature needs object storage, which some self-hosted installs do not have. Should the API process skip installing the module when storage is missing, and the UI check whether the S3 env var is set?
evals.expected_output: No on both: availability is the module's own decision from its own config and secrets (§3.3 way 4, §3.5, §6). The module is always installed; off refuses by name with a stable code, and its public config projects a boolean from that same answer, which the browser reads. The browser never recomputes from config leaves or secret presence, and the off state is opaque (contact support or administrator). States this rule is unbacked by lint today.

evals.prompt: An enterprise-only route in a core module checks the organization's plan in a tRPC middleware and throws if it is not Enterprise. Is that fine?
evals.expected_output: No: the plan gate is declared with withEntitlement(entitlement, { feature, when }) on the route or procedure (record §7, 'The plan gate is declared'), enforced by langwatch/no-hand-rolled-plan-gate; the framework asks after access and refuses 402 enterprise_plan_required. Enterprise routes stay mounted and refuse per organization (§11). If the code itself is enterprise-licensed it belongs in an enterprise module (langwatch/enterprise-license-header).

evals.prompt: feature-configuration fails on modules/langy/contract/src/langy.config.ts and says to export langyServerConfigSchema. Should I add it?
evals.expected_output: Flags a disagreement rather than complying: *ServerConfigSchema is a §15 deleted spelling and §6 teaches Config.define plus defineBrowserConfig, while the policy still demands the old export. Reports it to the coordinator or Alex as a linter-versus-record conflict instead of writing a deleted spelling or editing the policy.
